other_side: Zitron's argument is that the AI boom's revenue is mostly the labs and hyperscalers paying each other. He estimates that OpenAI and Anthropic are 70 to 80 per cent of AI compute demand, that 80 per cent of their enterprise revenue comes from 1 per cent of customers, and that those customers are largely venture-funded startups reselling tokens at a loss.
truth_beneath: The variable both men orbit is whether Anthropic's revenue is durable and broad. They accept the same facts: huge losses in 2025, very rapid growth since, and a heavy reliance on a few big customers. The empirical question is whether growth comes from many paying businesses with real return on investment or from venture-funded intermediaries, and the observable that settles it is the audited customer breadth, margin and retention in the IPO filing, plus whether enterprise token spend stops falling. The worldview residue is whether a ten-times growth rate extrapolates. For Whittemore to be right, the numbers must show diversified, sticky revenue. For Zitron to be right, concentration and subsidised usage must dominate and funding conditions tighten. Both are polemicists with incentives: Whittemore is bullish and anti-doom, Zitron is bubble-certain and anti-hype. The signal is where they agree despite opposite priors, that the filing, not the commentary, will tell us. Watch the customer concentration disclosures.
